newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Indonesia '97 palm oil output seen rising 14.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia '97 palm oil output seen rising 14.3 pct.

text.p: Indonesia's crude palm oil output in calendar 1997 is seen rising 14.3 percent to 5.6 million tonnes from 4.9 million tonnes in 1996, the vice-chairman of the Indonesian Palm Oil Producers Association (GAPKI) said on Thursday.
Derom Bangun said, however, that palm oil exports will only rise slightly to one million tonnes this year from 980,000 tonnes in 1996.
"CPO (crude palm oil) production should reach a total of 5.6 million tonnes this year," Bangun told Reuters in an interview at the Third Annual Edible Oil Markets conference in Singapore.
He said CPO output in the first half of 1997 should reach 2.3 million tonnes while exports over the same period are likely to hit 400,000 tonnes.
Indonesia is the world's second largest producer of palm oil and is aiming to dislodge Malaysia from the top spot in the next few years.
